The crystal is described in space group P6₃/m (number 176, Hall symbol –P 6c), using a hexagonal input cell with a = b = 8.25783175 Å, c = 5.704113 Å, α = β = 90°, and γ = 119.99999797°, essentially the ideal 120° hexagonal angle. The input cell contains 14 atoms with the declared composition Ba₆Os₂N₆, and all coordinates are fractional. The standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where P is effectively the identity matrix (its only departures from exact ones on the diagonal are at the 10⁻¹⁷ to 10⁻³² level) and the origin shift s is (1.0000000000287557×10⁻⁶, 1.0000000000287557×10⁻⁶, 0), so the input geometry is recovered by subtracting this shift from the standard-frame coordinates. Input positions were rounded to six decimal places before the listed corrections were derived.

Barium occupies the sixfold general-position orbit 6h with coordinate relation (x, y, 1/4), the representative atom sitting at x = 0.359446, y = 0.098532, z = 1/4; the two independent parameters x and y generate all six barium sites through the P6₃/m symmetry, with the orbit split between the z = 1/4 and z = 3/4 mirror-related layers. Osmium lies on the twofold special position 2c at the fixed coordinates (1/3, 2/3, 1/4), with no free parameters, its symmetry partner residing at (2/3, 1/3, 3/4). Nitrogen occupies a second, independent 6h orbit, distinct from the barium one, with representative position x = 0.118997, y = 0.684774, z = 1/4; these two free parameters likewise generate six nitrogen atoms distributed over the z = 1/4 and z = 3/4 planes. Thus the structure is built from three independent sublattices: a Ba 6h network, an Os 2c pair along the threefold axes at (1/3, 2/3) and (2/3, 1/3), and a separate N 6h network, all stacked in two crystallographic layers at heights one-quarter and three-quarters of the c axis.

Because the input coordinates were rounded to six decimals, small corrections are required to recover the exact symmetry-consistent geometry, and each must be applied to the stated pre-correction input position. For barium, the atom input at (0.901467, 0.260913, 0.25) is displaced by (+2×10⁻⁶, +2×10⁻⁶, 0); the atom at (0.739085, 0.640553, 0.25) is displaced by (0, +2×10⁻⁶, 0); the atom at (0.640553, 0.901467, 0.75) is displaced by (+2×10⁻⁶, +2×10⁻⁶, 0); and the atom at (0.260913, 0.359445, 0.75) is displaced by (+2×10⁻⁶, 0, 0). For osmium, the atom input at (0.333332, 0.666666, 0.25) is shifted by (+1×10⁻⁶, +1×10⁻⁶, 0), and its partner at (0.666666, 0.333332, 0.75) by (+1×10⁻⁶, +1×10⁻⁶, 0), bringing both onto the exact special-position values. For nitrogen, the atom at (0.118996, 0.684773, 0.25) is displaced by (0, +1×10⁻⁶, 0); the atom at (0.315225, 0.434222, 0.25) by (+1×10⁻⁶, 0, 0); the atom at (0.565776, 0.881002, 0.25) by (+2×10⁻⁶, +2×10⁻⁶, 0); the atom at (0.881002, 0.315225, 0.75) by (+2×10⁻⁶, +1×10⁻⁶, 0); and the atom at (0.684773, 0.565776, 0.75) by (+1×10⁻⁶, +2×10⁻⁶, 0). These corrections reflect rounding of the real input geometry rather than any idealization of the structure, and together with the stated lattice, symmetry, and orbit parameters they fully specify the atomic arrangement of this Ba₆Os₂N₆ cell.
